story.title: Support was the first job everyone tried to automate and got wrong.
body: The last decade’s answer was a widget in the corner of the page that asked you to rephrase your question four times and then offered to open a ticket. It did not save anyone money. It moved the cost onto the customer and called it self-service.

The mistake was in the framing. Support was treated as a cost to remove rather than a queue to clear. Once you decide the goal is fewer people, every product decision that follows is a small cruelty to somebody.

We started from the other end. A support queue is mostly the same fifteen questions, asked by people who are mildly annoyed and would like an answer before lunch. Almost none of it needs a person. The part that does needs a person badly, and needs them unhurried.
So Lapse takes the first part and protects the second. That is the whole idea, and everything in the product exists to keep those two halves separate.

rules.title: We will not build the version of this that replaces your team

items.text: We do not sell headcount reduction, and we will not put it in a proposal.

texture.alt: Folded fabric lit from the side

items.text: We do not charge per seat. Adding a teammate should never cost you money.
We publish what we refuse to automate, and the list gets longer, not shorter.
Every reply says it came from an agent. That is not a setting.
